newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Technical bounce pushes Seoul shrs to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Technical bounce pushes Seoul shrs to higher close.

text.p: Seoul shares closed highre on Wednesday due to a broad-based technical rebound after three consecutive days of falls, brokers said.
Buying was also active in advance of Thursday's deadline for the settlement of March futures contracts as investors tried to cover short positions, they said.
The composite stock index ended 7.95 points higher to a provisional 663.90. Advancing shares beat decliners 424 to 371, while 29.99 million shares changed hands.
"The market especially advanced in the last minutes, likely due to futures-related buying," an LG Securities broker said.
The March futures contracts closed 0.90 of a point higher at 66.80, while their underlying KOSPI 200 index rose 0.69 of a point to 66.83.
But brokers said profit-taking was likely to emerge on Thursday as fundamentals remained weak. Soaring interest rates and a weakening won are undermining the market sentiment.
Heavily index-weighted large-cap shares led the market's gains. Hyundai Motor jumped 1,600 won to 24,500 and Korean Air rose 700 won to 14,000.
Chip stocks also closed higher, boosted by hopes that global semiconductor prices were recovering.
Samsung Electronics gained 1,700 won to 53,700. Hyundai Electronics climbed 2,000 won to 34,000.
Brokers said selling by foreigners appeared to be slowing. Recently, foreigners have been net sellers of construction and banking stocks.

A Federation of Korean Industries statement on Tuesday that it may intervene in Shindongbang's hostile takeover bid for Midopa disappointed investors. Midopa and its parent Dainong fell to their lower limits of 29,900 won (down 2,500) and 7,120 won (down 610), respectively. Shindongbang slid 1,500 won to 35,500.
